rationale: Follow-up to the accepted BN-fold bundle trial-a7f5de7ac7-param-23c435d4 (objective 3.6458 ms vs parent 4.2489 ms, quality pass, decision accepted). inputs/previous-feedback.txt changes this attempt in four measured ways rather than reporting a failure to repair. (1) It records the accepted trial's clean runtime evidence: candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6 shows zero handled exceptions and zero False-returning predicates, all 17 inherited sites were covered (count 2), and nsys-9ed9145c independently corroborated the candidate-declared routes (19 scudnn/winograd conv kernels, 3 bn_fw_inf, 8+8 elementwise add/relu kernels, 70/70 CUDA kernels associated) - so the fold + fused-conv-relu pattern is re-implemented as the trusted base. (2) binding_cost-2087a4f7 measured whole-invocation parent-vs-passthrough deltas of only 0.013/0.036 ms for the accepted bundle's module hooks, and python_runtime-aea48e29 shows the invocation is GPU-bound (1.375 of 3.92 ms cProfile wall self in _cuda_synchronize; dispatch self times 0.33-0.46 ms hidden under GPU execution), so re-partitioning 17 module sites into 12 boundaries (8 ResNetBasicLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut + 1 ResNetEmbeddings) keeps binding cost second-order and latency must come from removing GPU kernel work. (3) The same collector inventories quantify the remaining unfused GPU work this candidate targets: 8 aten.add_ (78.3 us) + 8 aten.relu (62.3 us) + 3 shortcut eval-BatchNorm kernels (26.4 us) = 167.0 us of the 3503.8 us diagnostic CUDA total, plus the 8 layer[1] plain conv2d sites (1459.8 us) whose fused-epilogue engine family measured faster per shape (accepted parameter search: cudnn_conv_relu 3.6435 ms vs conv2d_folded 4.2335 ms project latency; per-shape 128ch@28 149.1 vs 160.4 us, 64ch@56 230.3 vs 238.7 us, 256ch@14 163.6 vs 166.6 us, 512ch@7 160.8 vs 164.3 us). (4) No collector output prescribes a failure route, so the attempt extends the measured-good base. Design (joint, exactly the 13 selected groups): the earlier bundle is explicitly replaced as a whole (replaces: trial-a7f5de7ac7-param-23c435d4) because owning the layer[1] conv kernel is only legal with ownership of all inherited folded boundaries - this bundle re-implements all 17 folded sites (stem via the embeddings boundary). Each ResNetBasicLayer boundary runs layer[0] as one aten.cudnn_convolution_relu on folded weights (the accepted implementation), obtains the residual by calling self.shortcut exactly like the parent (the 5 nn.Identity shortcut module calls stay parent calls; the 3 ResNetShortCut sites run this bundle's folded conv+bias single kernel), and evaluates layer[1] + residual add + final ReLU as one aten.cudnn_convolution_add_relu(h, W1', z=residual, alpha=1.0, bias=b1') call - the op exists in the worker torch 2.13.0+cu129 with schema verified. The ResNetEmbeddings boundary runs the accepted fused stem conv+relu and then the parent MaxPool2d module call unchanged. Numerics: cudnn_convolution_add_relu computes relu(conv(x,W',b') + 1.0*z) with the same fp32 single-rounding convolution accumulation as the parent's conv -> add_ -> relu sequence, and the BN fold is the accepted ~1e-7-relative reassociation, so the frozen atol=rtol=1e-4 logits comparison with exact top-1 is expected to hold (CPU simulation of every route including all fallbacks matches the pristine parent model to 2.5e-06 with identical argmax). Every fused site keeps the accepted guard ladder - one synchronized installation probe (deterministic linspace tensors, no RNG consumption), per-site runtime latch to the kernel-for-kernel parent sequence conv2d(W',b')+add_+relu, then parent forward for unsupported signature/dtype/device/training/grad contexts, with setup-failure, unsupported-signature and runtime-failure kept as distinct route labels - and an epilogue_route parameter lets TaskSearch compare the fused and unfused routes on paired project measurements. No CUDA graphs, no functional dispatch (module-boundary callables only, binding stays legacy/direct), no capture of fixture outputs; the workload executes on current inputs on every invocation. Expectation (hypothesis from diagnostic CUDA durations, not a measured clean timing): removing ~167 us of kernel time and possibly moving the 8 layer[1] sites onto the fused-epilogue family gives roughly 0.15-0.26 ms off 3.6458 ms (4-7%), 8-15x the previous MAD-derived noise bounds (0.014-0.021 ms), with images_per_second rising further above the 7150.1 floor; the framework's independent paired measurement decides acceptance.

setup_work.where: build() at installation, after adapter.prepare() and before validation; never inside the timed invocation
steps: 1. Classify the selected module sites structurally (embeddings / basic layer / shortcut); ResNetConvLayer modules present in the selection's groups are deliberately not claimed - their computation is re-implemented inside the embeddings and block boundaries and their call IDs are listed in eliminated_calls.

2. Per physical conv module (17 conv-layer convs + 3 shortcut 1x1 convs), fold eval BatchNorm2d into the conv in float64 and cast to contiguous float32 packed tensors (W', b'): s = gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W' = W*s, b' = beta - mu*s [+ conv_bias*s]. Packed once per physical module and shared between boundary callables; original parameter tensors are untouched so every parent fallback recomputes the exact original parent computation.

3. Two one-time installation probes on the packed device: aten.cudnn_convolution_relu and aten.cudnn_convolution_add_relu on 16x16 deterministic linspace tensors, numerically verified against relu(conv+bias) / relu(conv+bias+1.0*z) and synchronized so setup-level declines surface at installation; a decline latches the kernel-for-kernel fallback sequences (kept as a distinct setup-failure route category).

retained_setup_memory.detail: 11,166,912 folded weight floats + 4,800 folded bias floats (20 convs: stem 7x7, 16 block 3x3, 3 shortcut 1x1) retained for the invocation lifetime; counted in framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes (which includes installation) and framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes, not in the per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes counter that is reset for each run.

setup_work.transient_setup_memory: float64 folding intermediates bounded by the largest single conv (512x512x3x3 ~18.9 MB), freed during setup; probes allocate a few KB; no inference-mode tensors are created (no_grad only), no CUDA graphs or graph pools, no RNG consumption (linspace only), no changes to batch/sequence/sampling semantics.
setup_work.expected_run_memory_effect: Per-run peak_allocated should fall versus the current parent (301,621,760 bytes at the accepted trial): each block's post-add ReLU output and each shortcut's eval-BN output no longer exist as separate tensors (~96 MB of block ReLU outputs + ~22 MB of shortcut BN outputs per forward before allocator reuse). This is a PyTorch allocator counter change over the replaced boundaries, not a claim of general physical-memory saving; peak_allocated_bytes stays a non-objective metric under the 0.95 throughput floor.

quality_risks: cudnn 9.20 may not service the fused conv+add+relu graph for every FP32 NCHW shape or engine choice; mitigation is the accepted pattern - one synchronized installation probe plus a per-site runtime latch to conv2d(W',b')+add_+relu_ (kernel-for-kernel the current parent behavior, bounding each site at current cost), plus the epilogue_route parameter so TaskSearch compares routes on paired project measurements.

A fused engine could be slower than the unfused pair on an individual shape (notably 64ch@56 with z); the per-site latch and the route parameter expose and bound this, and the framework's paired project measurement decides acceptance.

Numerical: the fused epilogue and the BN fold reassociate fp32 rounding (expected ~1e-6-scale differences; CPU-simulated worst case 2.5e-06 across all routes); gated by the frozen atol=rtol=1e-4 logits comparison, exact top-1, and observe()'s repeated-forward closeness check, which runs the same replaced path.

Coverage: the 12 declared boundaries execute on every invocation; the 17 inherited conv-layer sites and the other eliminated inner calls no longer execute and are listed in eliminated_calls because their computation is re-implemented inside the replaced boundaries (the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced). If any boundary hits an unsupported context it falls back to the parent forward and the original inner calls execute unchanged.

In-place semantics: the parent mutates layer[1]'s conv output with add_; that intermediate is a Sequential-local value with no external aliases (verified against the transformers 5.16.1 source), so returning a fresh fused-output tensor is value- and alias-equivalent for all consumers; the residual z is only read, never written, matching the parent which never mutates the residual.

params.name: epilogue_route
params.description: Implementation route for the 8 residual-block epilogues (layer[1] conv + residual add + final ReLU): 'cudnn_conv_add_relu' evaluates each epilogue as one aten.cudnn_convolution_add_relu kernel on folded weights; 'conv2d_add_relu' evaluates conv2d(W', b') + add_ + relu, kernel-for-kernel the current accepted parent behavior. Both routes share the identical BN fold, FP32 policy (TF32 off, benchmark off), workload, sampling and thresholds; the choice only selects between two legal implementations of the same computation. Read from context['parameters'] at build time; default 'cudnn_conv_add_relu'. The stem/layer[0] fused conv+relu route is unchanged by this parameter (the accepted trial already measured it faster).
